summary: OpenAI announced Patch the Planet, a Daybreak initiative with Trail of Bits, HackerOne and Calif that pairs frontier cyber-capable models (Codex Security, GPT-5.5-Cyber) with human security engineers to find and help patch vulnerabilities in widely used open-source projects such as cURL, the Go project, Python and OpenSSL-adjacent libraries.

practices.reason: Describes concrete agentic workflows -- repeated Codex /goal runs to build fuzzing labs, a CVE-history-driven variant-search pipeline with judging agents, and Codex-generated shim code for cross-implementation differential testing -- with stated time savings an engineering team could replicate.
practices.quote: Trail of Bits engineers used repeated Codex /goal runs with GPT‑5.5‑Cyber to build an entire fuzzing lab covering dozens of entry points, variant builds, platforms, and novel test seeds ... The completed setup took less than a day. Trail of Bits estimates that building the same lab manually would ordinarily take at least several weeks.

practices.reason: Lays out a triage methodology -- human security engineers reproducing evidence, deduplicating, reassessing severity and filtering false positives -- that a team could adapt when deciding whether to trust AI-generated vulnerability findings before acting on them.
practices.quote: While frontier AI models are highly capable of finding vulnerabilities and patching them, they also produce a high volume of false positives that can contribute to the already overwhelming backlog maintainers are facing. Patch the Planet solves for this by having dedicated Trail of Bits researchers reproduce the evidence, check findings against project-specific documentation and threat models, remove duplicates, reassess severity, and prioritize confirmed vulnerabilities for remediation.

notable_reason: Documents concrete, large-scale AI-assisted discovery of serious real-world vulnerabilities -- including a 23-year-old OpenBSD privilege-escalation bug, dozens of Linux kernel LPE PoCs, and a Firefox 0-day that forced Pwn2Own withdrawals -- which is a significant demonstration of frontier model cyber capability.
